messages:
nisha: FYI customer frankie-inc reported a big trial credit drop overnight, ~9.8k tokens gone. they say no UI traffic, just our nightly sync job.
liam: which API were they hitting? embeddings / rerank / chat?
nisha: embeddings. scheduled nightly job that batches doc inserts. job id sync_0x9c, runs in background on our worker pool. logs show lots of retries + 'cancelled' states.
jordan: can you paste the job logs / trace id?
nisha: pasted below — trimmed
```
2026-03-15T03:11:58Z worker-7 INFO starting sync job sync_0x9c attempt=1 trace=tr-44a
2026-03-15T03:12:05Z worker-7 ERROR network error during /v1/embeddings call request_id=req-f7a
2026-03-15T03:12:06Z worker-7 INFO enqueue retry attempt=2
2026-03-15T03:12:07Z worker-3 INFO sync job sync_0x9c attempt=2 started trace=tr-44a
2026-03-15T03:12:07Z worker-3 INFO sent batch=42 payload_hash=0x9ef request_id=req-f7a
2026-03-15T03:12:08Z worker-3 INFO received 200 for req-f7a; kvcache saved
2026-03-15T03:12:08Z worker-7 INFO late response received for same payload request_id=req-f7a duplicate
```

nisha: you can see both workers retried the same payload without idempotency key -> double bill.
maria: do we have idempotency header in the SDK for background jobs? I thought embeddings accepted X-Request-ID but not enforced.
liam: SDK sets a client-generated id if provided, but many customers use server-side schedulers that don't set it. our ingestion lib has dedupe via local lease but if the process dies and restarts we lose it.
jordan: sounds like a saga/lease race. worker-7 thought job failed and retried, worker-3 had resumed and completed too. billing counts both successful embedding responses.
ops-bot: alert created INC-2217: "background sync duplicate embeddings causing trial burn" assigned to eng-ml.
nisha: customer says promo credits weren't applied on those requests either — so platform billed trial balance first then regular. they saw immediate balance drop.
billing-bot: created refund ticket RF-8932 for frankie-inc for 9800 tokens; pending manual review.
maria: quick mitigation: pause their scheduled sync, flip scheduler to single-worker affinity, enable idempotency header injection in client wrapper.
liam: also add a short-term server-side dedupe: if we see identical payload_hash + account_id within 30s, drop/ack subsequent requests and return cached embedding id. low risk and fixes cases like this.
jordan: repro steps I used locally:
1) start sync worker A processing batch X
2) inject `SIGTERM` to A while request outstanding
3) allow coordinator to spawn worker B immediately
4) B re-sends same batch without idempotency header
5) both responses succeed -> double-count
snippet of repro script:
```
# simulate kill-and-restart
python -m tooling/sim_sync --batch 42 --account frankie-inc &
sleep 1; kill -SIGTERM $!
# spawn a new worker that doesn't have previous lease
python -m tooling/sim_sync --batch 42 --account frankie-inc
```

nisha: customer asked for an ETA on refunds + fix. what's reasonable?
maria: refund ticket in billing queue, manual review may take 24-48h. engineering hotfix (server-side dedupe + scheduler affinity) could be in a patch within 48h if we prioritize.
liam: low-risk temporary change: on embeddings endpoint, if payload_hash+account seen in last 60s, return cached response with header `X-Redwood-Dedup: true`. I'll draft PR today.
ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary for dedupe middleware in staging at 2026-03-15T17:30Z.
jordan: also recommend alerts on sudden overnight trial depletion for accounts with only background jobs — can surface earlier.
nisha: reply to customer: paused their nightly job, refund ticket created, engineering working on dedupe hotfix. thanks all :heart:
maria: will follow up once RF-8932 cleared and PR merged.
liam: assigning myself to the PR and follow-up on billing refund. ping me if regressions.
billing-bot: RF-8932 status updated -> pending-approval by finance.
ops-bot: INC-2217 updated: root cause suspected: lack of idempotency + scheduler race. next action: implement server-side dedupe + SDK guidance doc.
support: tagging for postmortem once resolved."
